correctness.rationale: All essential inferences, boundary conditions and computations in DRAFT.md (interval 180<=RT(30,K4,6)<=255 + circulant optimality) were independently re-verified. Lower bound: J={4,5,6,8,10,13} on Z30 is disjoint from -J mod 30 and excludes 15, so C30(J) is simple 12-regular with 30*12/2=180 edges; rebuilt matrix byte-identical to artifacts/best_adj.txt. Standalone verifier re-run reports edges=180, 12-regular, K4 check passed (27405 quadruples), alpha<=5 passed (593775 6-sets), VERIFIED. Cross-checked by independent code paths: triangle-extension K4 search (no K4), bitmask branch-and-bound max-independent computation gives alpha=5 exactly, and all 12 catalog jump sets verified K4-free and alpha<=5 via search.py exact routines. Upper bound: Lemma 2 proof is logically valid conditional on external R(3,6)<=18: if d(v)>=18 then N(v) (>=18 vertices) is triangle-free (else triangle+N(v)+v=K4) so by R(3,6)=18 contains I6, contradicting alpha<=5; hence Delta<=17 and e<=30*17/2=255. Arithmetic, binomial counts (C(30,4)=27405, C(30,6)=593775, C(14,6)=3003, C(14,7)=3432, C(14,8)=3003, C(14,9)=2002, C(14,10)=1001), Turan numbers T(30,3)=435-3*C(10,2)=300 and Turan(30,5)=435-5*C(6,2)=360 (so complement bound e>=75), and n^2/8=112.5 all re-derived correctly. Circulant optimality: full re-run of circulant_enum.py in 5.3s reproduces claimed counts exactly (k=6:3003 total/12 feasible; k=7:3432/170 K4-free/0 feasible; k=8:3003/49/0; k=9:2002/10/0; k=10:1001/1/0; k=6+15:3003/64/0; k=7+15:3432/8/0; k=8+15:3003/0/0). Method is sound: K4 exact enumeration for rejection/acceptance, greedy I6 finding is sound for rejection (any returned 6-set is by construction independent, certifying alpha>=6), exact 593775-set check required for acceptance, so no false feasible/infeasible. Coverage complete: even k<=5 and odd k<=5+15 have <180 edges and cannot beat witness; computed degrees 12-17; degree>=18 cases (k>=9 even degree>=18, k>=9+15 degree>=19) correctly discharged by Lemma 2 contrapositive; k=9 even and k=10 even computed redundantly. Honesty section correctly disclaims SAT/DRAT, exact m*, and global enumeration. No proof-vs-evidence confusion: lower bound and circulant classification are machine-checked proofs by complete enumeration (replayable in seconds), upper bound is deductive proof modulo cited R(3,6). External citation R(3,6)=18 and R(4,6) in [36,41] consistent with cutoff textbook knowledge; attribution to Greenwood-Gleason 1955 not live-verified but fact is standard. No correctness defect requiring repair.

originality.rationale: Substantive comparison shows no prior result anticipates the specific combined claim. Internal SCOPE Resultary (001: 4-uniform 1-forbidden max 17 on 8 points; 003: J2-free binary rank to n<=5; 002: spider walk mixing) differs in objects, claim types and methods; failed lanes (Szemeredi-Trotter 4x4, dicyclic spectral gaps, Polya-Vinogradov) are disjoint. Topic-listed nearest externals are disjoint: (i) SAT+CAS certificates for R(3,8)=28/R(3,9)=36 treat triangle-vs-clique decision, not K4-free edge-maximization under alpha<=5; (ii) SAT Ramsey-type grid/vdW work provides only satisfiable witnesses, no UNSAT upper bound for K4/alpha and no RT table; (iii) bipartite Turan subdivision asymptotics O(n^{1+1/k-1/sk}) contain no n<=32 exact values; (iv) monochromatic-cycle Ramsey-Turan variant is asymptotic/structural, not RT(n,K4,k) exact. Classical Turan ex(30,K4)=300 and R(3,6)=18 are prior but DRAFT explicitly marks Lemma 2 as folklore, claiming novelty only for the explicit 180-edge circulant interval and reusable circulant-optimum benchmark in the R(4,6)-gap regime (n=30 inside open [36,41], not adjacent to solved R(4,5)=25). No surveyed source contains an RT(30,K4,6) table entry. Attempted live primary-source fetches (mathworld RamseyNumber, arxiv 2502.06055, arxiv 1001.2078) failed with transport errors, so priority cannot be established by timestamp; assessment rests on substantive disjointness and cutoff knowledge that small-n RT exact tables are absent from asymptotic RT literature. Residual risk of an unpublished folklore circulant in Ramsey databases remains, but no substantive anticipation found. Hence narrowly PASS on originality (new, even if weak); value is assessed separately.

value.rationale: Even though correct and narrowly new, the result as stated is not independently worth finding later. Target was exact RT(30,K4,6)=m* with DRAT UNSAT certificate plus extremal enumeration; fallback required interval width <=8 with SAT evidence and near-extremal catalog. Delivered gap is 75 (180 vs 255, ~42% relative), ~10x fallback width, with no SAT CNF built, no UNSAT certificate, and no global enumeration — explicitly disclaimed in Sec.6. Upper bound U=255 is a one-line folklore corollary of cited R(3,6) (Delta<=17), shaving only 45 from trivial Turan 300, leaving the hard upper-bound work untouched. Lower bound 180 (+105 over trivial complement-Turan 75, exceeding n^2/8~=112.5) is a single computer-found circulant with no structural theory explaining why it works or how far from optimal it is. Theorem 2 (optimality among circulants) exhausts only ~20k labeled circulants out of 2^435 graphs — a negligible, theoretically unmotivated slice chosen for search convenience — and therefore does not constrain the global optimum, which may lie anywhere in 181-255. The 12 jump sets are listed without insight (unexplained enumeration), and the interval does not bridge asymptotic RT(n,K4,o(n))~n^2/8 theory to machine-checkable practice nor provide a tight seed: future exact work must still close 75 edges including the SAT-hard 181+ UNSAT. Quantitative improvement over trivial 75-300 is real but leaves a preliminary benchmark, not a substantive advance. This matches rejection categories: textbook restatement (upper bound) + unexplained enumeration (circulant catalog) with a wide, uncertified gap. Hence FAIL on value, requiring overall REJECT per policy (originality/value failure must be REJECT, not REPAIRABLE).
